gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EasySMX's own X05 Pro listing calls its D-pad a 'tactile microswitch' (GamingOnLinux heard 'a clear click'), so the $35.99 X05 Pro is quiet on face buttons, bumpers and triggers but not on the D-pad, while the $49.99 GameSir Super Nova's maker claims silence only for the ABXY buttons.
standout_why: The hlplanet G7 vs G7 SE page (cited) covers GameSir only: G7 SE membrane at $44.99, G7 Pro at $79.99 and Cyclone 2 at $55.99. It has no EasySMX, Sony or Mobapad model and nothing about D-pads. The hlplanet under-$20 page gives button types but says nothing about noise. The cited manuals.plus Super Nova PDF returned no readable text through the fetch tool. I could not open either Reddit thread (r/Controller 'Quietest controllers', 'Quiet Controller Recommendation… X05 Pro') because WebFetch is blocked on reddit.com, so I can't rule out a comment mentioning the D-pad click. In ChatGPT's answer the X05 Pro has a 'silicone-damped… D-pad', and our current page says 'Face buttons, D-pad, bumpers, triggers all damped'. Both conflict with the maker's own text.
decides: This confirms the EasySMX X05 Pro as the cheapest pick with quiet buttons at $35.99, $14 less than the Super Nova and the Mobapad Chitu 2 Silent. Our 'What is quiet' cell must change: face buttons, bumpers and triggers are damped, but the D-pad is a microswitch with a soft click and L3/R3 also click. Shoppers who lean on the D-pad (platformers, fighting games) should be pointed to the EasySMX S05 Pro ($54.99, silicone-damped buttons plus a 'smooth disc-pivot D-pad', Switch-focused).
